review.mandate_note: Page 49 says the President should keep EO 12866 as the basis of OIRA review and that regulatory analysis and OIRA review should also be required of historically independent agencies, citing an OLC finding; paraphrase is accurate.

source_checks.note: EO 14215 signed 2025-02-18, 90 FR 10447: all agencies including independent ones must submit significant regulatory actions to OIRA; EO 12866's agency definition rewritten to include the FEC; Federal Reserve monetary policy excluded; submissions start within 60 days or on completion of OMB guidance.

M-25-24 dated 2025-04-17 (acting OIRA Administrator): full EO 12866 compliance by 2025-04-21, covering rules and guidance documents; agencies should plan for up to 90 days of review; lists SEC, FCC, FTC, NLRB and others.
Trump v. Slaughter, No. 25-332, decided 2026-06-29, 6-3: FTC for-cause removal protection unconstitutional; Federal Reserve status expressly not resolved (fetched for c03-07).

significance.rationale: Extending OIRA review to independent agencies adds a process step across regulators that oversee large parts of the economy.

status_summary: EO 14215 (signed 2025-02-18) requires independent regulatory agencies to submit significant regulatory actions to OIRA before publication, amends the EO 12866 definition of agency to cover the Federal Election Commission, and keeps the Federal Reserve's monetary-policy functions outside. OMB memorandum M-25-24 (2025-04-17) required agencies such as the SEC, FCC, FTC and NLRB to comply by 2025-04-21, with significant actions generally receiving up to 90 days of review. The Supreme Court's 2026-06-29 decision in Trump v. Slaughter, which held FTC commissioners removable at will, strengthens the President's control of such agencies but does not itself concern OIRA review.

timeline.event: EO 14215 signed (published 2025-02-24, 90 FR 10447): independent agencies must submit proposed and final significant regulatory actions to OIRA; OMB to issue guidance; Federal Reserve monetary policy excluded.

OMB memorandum M-25-24 issued by the acting OIRA Administrator: independent agencies must designate regulatory contacts and begin full EO 12866 compliance by 2025-04-21, covering rules and certain guidance documents.

Communications Daily reports that FCC rulemakings are now subject to OIRA review since 2025-04-21, with experts expecting a mostly procedural effect given alignment between the White House and the FCC chair.

The Supreme Court decides Trump v. Slaughter 6-3, holding the FTC's for-cause removal protection unconstitutional and overruling Humphrey's Executor in substance; the Federal Reserve is treated separately.

title: Require OIRA review of rules from historically independent agencies
